eipi.notes: Mostly a single big formula pair (d/dt e^kt = k e^kt, e^0=1) over a number line or complex plane that keeps one equation stable for 30-60 s; very sparse, ends with pi creature and e^i pi = -1.

de1.notes: Mostly pictures: phase-space plots, pendulum and three-body animations with one equation shown at a time; formulas arrive singly and stay while the picture evolves, with pi-creature skits at section boundaries; the code editor segment and end credits add blank-ish tiles.

de4.notes: Dense with moving pictures (epicycle drawings, temperature surfaces, complex-plane circles) and mostly one or two formulas on screen at a time; formula blocks build up cumulatively for 20-60 s (Fourier coefficient derivation), and the sequence ends with a text-heavy challenge slide and credits.

clt.notes: Heavy picture content: Galton-board photos and simulations, histograms and dice grids dominate; formulas arrive one at a time and rarely more than 3-5 at once, with pi-creature dialogue breaks between sections.

l10ch6.notes: Our chapter is one equation or a few lines at a time on a mostly dark screen, with a plane/pendulum picture on the left; derivation lines are stacked cumulatively (3-6 at once) and many frames are pure text/maths; picture density is low (1-2) and tiles are clean.

l12ch1.notes: Our video is clean maths: one or two formula blocks growing cumulatively (derivation stacks of 4-7 lines), few pictures, plenty of coloured-text prose boxes; screen is mostly dark with text/maths centred, and the formula lines persist for several tiles.
